Presentation Format Showdown

HTML Slides vs. PowerPoint: A Better Way to Present

Comparing modern web-based slides against the legacy standard — responsiveness, accessibility, and delivery in the browser age

The Problem

PowerPoint's 30-year-old format still constrains how we persuade and decide

Presentations are a primary vehicle for decision-making — yet the tooling hasn't kept up

  • Font substitution: carefully chosen typography breaks the moment a file moves to another machine
  • Fixed-resolution layouts: slides designed at one size distort on different screens and projectors
  • Bloated file sizes: the average corporate .pptx weighs 8–15 MB; an equivalent HTML deck fits under 1 MB
  • Version-control headaches: binary files can't be meaningfully diffed, merged, or tracked in git
PowerPoint's legacy architecture imposes real limits on presentation quality — the format, not the presenter, is the bottleneck.

The Modern Alternative

Your browser is already a presentation engine

HTML slides are full presentations built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript — rendered natively in any browser

  • Reveal.js — the most popular open-source framework with rich transitions and plugin support
  • Slidev — developer-friendly, Markdown-driven slides powered by Vue
  • Marp — converts Markdown to slide decks with a minimal, clean workflow
  • Impress.js — CSS3 transforms for cinematic, spatial presentations
HTML slides turn the browser into a full-featured, universally available presentation platform.

Responsive design

HTML slides adapt to every screen — PowerPoint doesn't

98% of devices worldwide run a modern browser, making HTML the universal canvas

  • Fluid layout: HTML reflows text, charts, and images to fit any viewport — laptop, tablet, phone, or projector
  • Fixed canvas trap: PowerPoint locks every element to a 13.3 × 7.5″ rectangle, cropping or stretching on non-standard screens
  • Zero manual work: No duplicate decks for different devices — one file renders everywhere

Typography & Design Fidelity

CSS delivers pixel-perfect typography that PowerPoint cannot guarantee

No more "missing font" surprises when you present on a different machine

  • Web fonts load reliably — CSS @font-face guarantees every viewer sees the exact typeface you chose
  • Precise kerning & line-height — sub-pixel rendering, letter-spacing, and line-height are enforced by the browser engine
  • No font-substitution problem — PowerPoint silently swaps missing fonts, breaking layout and brand consistency
  • Font embedding bloat eliminated — .pptx files embed entire font binaries; HTML links only the weights you use

Key Considerations

  • Version control: Every change is tracked in Git with full history, branching, and blame
  • Pull requests & diff reviews: Teammates review exact line-level changes — no "Final_v3_REAL.pptx"
  • CI/CD pipelines: Lint, test, and auto-deploy on every merge — zero manual export steps
  • Distribution is a link: Share a URL instead of attaching a 15 MB file that clogs inboxes

Accessibility

HTML delivers WCAG 2.1 AA natively — PowerPoint bolts it on after the fact

Semantic elements and ARIA give HTML slides built-in accessibility that .pptx can only approximate

  • Semantic tags — headings, lists, and landmarks are native to HTML, giving screen readers a structured document out of the box
  • ARIA attributes — fine-grained roles, states, and labels let authors describe any interactive element
  • Keyboard navigation — tab order and focus management are browser primitives, not add-ons
  • PowerPoint's checker — runs post-hoc, flags issues after content is built, and cannot enforce semantic structure
HTML supports WCAG 2.1 AA natively via semantic elements and ARIA — W3C WAI guidelines
